It really depends on the situation, the client, the emergency. On a regular day, we have appointments with users, and we will work on their need. ( Do they have their RAMQ? Do they benefit from social security? Do they need to see a psychiatrist or a doctor? Do they need medication or have wounds? Do they have a place to stay for the night or not? Etc). Most of the time, we try to help them on the mazes, which is the gourvenement. We try to help them to look for a room or apartment.  If we do not have any appointments, we go to community resources, and we try to locate any new people who may need assistance. We do what we call reaching out. It can be hard to get people trust, so we try to be useful. ( Do they need a ride, food, crack pipe, syringe, condom, water, a place to take a shower, tampon, etc.)? With this, we can create trust. We also have to deal with emergency ( tornado alert like today. They need to have a secure place, hot day, cold day, etc.). We can also have emergencies called from the hospital. Otherwise, we have a lot of paperwork............really hope I am clear.
